answer: Try concurrent bandwidth probes. Each epoch a verifier picks a random batch of accounts and, in the same second, streams each one a 50 MB random blob to hash and echo back. Agents on separate links finish in about 4 seconds. Sybils sharing one uplink split the pipe, so twenty of them crawl past 80 seconds and miss the cutoff. To pass, a farmer must rent a separate 100 Mbps server per fake, around $5 a month each, so 1,000 sybils cost $5,000 monthly before earning a coin. Think of a narrow bridge over a reef: one raven glides across fast, but a whole flock jams and gets counted.
